newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel demands an end to attacks in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel demands an end to attacks in Bosnia.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Sunday attacks on international organisations in the Serb-controlled part of Bosnia had to stop immediately.

U.N. officials have criticised a recent series of Serb retaliatory attacks over increased international efforts to bring indicted war criminals to justice which led to a NATO swoop earlier this month on two Bosnian Serb suspects.
The bomb attacks have targeted U.S. forces and international monitors with the United Nations and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe. None have caused injury.

"Violent acts in the Republika Srpska (Serb Republic inside Bosnia) and attacks on the headquarters of international organisations must cease without delay," Kinkel said in an unusually harshly-worded ministry statement two days after visiting the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.

"It's outrageous that those who want to help are being attacked. It is incompatible to ask for aid at the Brussels donor conference and at the same time mount attacks on those helping at home," it quoted him as saying.

Kinkel said Serb-controlled Bosnia was increasingly isolating itself because former Bosnian Serb president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic was still at large and pulling political strings in the background.
Diplomats say peace can not be properly established until the former foes in the 1992-95 Bosnian war hand over suspected war criminals.
Refugee agencies say this is essential to instil confidence in Bosnian refugees that it is safe for them to return home.
The minister renewed his call on the Bosnian Serbs to hand Karadzic over to be tried by the United Nations war crimes tribunal in The Hague.
"He (Karadzic) is primarily to blame for the fact that the people there are living so badly. Some one should tell them that. He must get out of there, he belongs at The Hague tribunal," Kinkel said.
Citing World Bank figures, Kinkel said economic growth in the Moslem-Croat Federation, which makes up half of Bosnia, had grown by 50 percent while it had stagnated in the Serb part of the country.
"There has been zero (economic) growth in the Republika Srpska. Unemployment there is at about 80-90 percent. The media, which demonise the West, are manipulated," Kinkel said.

"The truth is that there is no world conspiracy against the Serbs. On the contrary, they should and must take their place within Europe. But this is something those responsible in Pale (Bosnian Serb capital) are trying to prevent."
